construction.fluent: whole script in one synthesis; reference transcript known, per-word reference timings do not exist — timing recorded not_scored, WER scored
construction.word_by_word: each token synthesized alone and concatenated with fixed silence gaps; reference word timings computed from the sample counts of the clips actually concatenated — exact by construction

fixtures.name: fox_pangram
fixtures.notes: The classic pangram; short function words (the, over) are the timing stress — easy for a transcriber to merge or drop. All 9 words exact; the start MAE (~0.31 s) is the systematic DTW onset lag this corpus exists to record, not noise.
fixtures.text: the quick brown fox jumps over the lazy dog

fixtures.name: market_morning
fixtures.notes: Sibilant-heavy opening — a real WER trap, and it springs: tiny.en heard 'Chi, cells, fresh, bread, bed, the, market, every morning' (she→Chi, sells→cells, at→bed; 3 substitutions of 9). The floor sits one further error above the measured value; a bigger STT model should beat this number, never hide it.
fixtures.text: she sells fresh bread at the market every morning

fixtures.name: small_tools
fixtures.notes: Plain declarative sentence, mid-length words. Perfect transcript; start MAE again ~0.31 s (the same systematic onset lag as fox_pangram).
fixtures.text: we build small tools that solve real problems

fixtures.name: tin_roof
fixtures.notes: Two 'the'-class function words plus a hard/rain consonant cluster. All 10 words exact.
fixtures.text: the rain fell hard on the tin roof last night

fixtures.name: water_plants
fixtures.notes: Polite-imperative phrasing; 'please' and 'before' are the words small models most often soften — tiny.en held both here.
fixtures.text: please remember to water the plants before you leave

floor_rule: WER floors sit one extra word error above the measured value on the shortest fixture (0.15 over a measured 0.0; 0.45 over market_morning's measured 0.3333). MAE floors sit ~1.5x the worst measured value (start 0.306 -> 0.45; end 0.2438 -> 0.40): the start-MAE cluster (~0.27-0.31 s on every word_by_word fixture) is a systematic onset lag of the measured STT rung on isolated words, so the floor guards regression of the rung, not the lag's existence. A machine whose STT rung is a larger whisper model should measure strictly better; floors are regression lines, not targets.

history.note: Corpus first runs caught a live defect in the TTS rung it measures through: PiperBackend.synthesize's fallback drove the pre-1.3 piper API (synthesize_stream_raw, then an unconfigured wave writer) — on current piper-tts every piper synthesis died with wave.Error '# channels not specified'. Fixed in tts.py: the current AudioChunk API is driven first, legacy APIs remain as fallbacks.

The corpus's second run (warm segment cache) caught a worse one: tts._to_int16 treated the SegmentCache's stdlib array('h') int16 samples as float amplitudes, clipping every nonzero sample to +/-32767 — every cache-hit speak() wrote a square wave (the run scored WER 2.0 against it). Fixed with dtype-aware scaling in _to_int16; post-fix runs are score-identical warm or cold. Note the disk cache entries themselves were always clean PCM (SegmentCache.put writes raw samples); only the write-out path was corrupt.

Piper alignment probe, recorded so nobody re-claims it from the API surface alone: piper-tts 1.3's synthesize/synthesize_wav accept include_alignments=True, but with the standard en_US-lessac-medium voice the chunks' phoneme_alignments and phoneme_id_samples come back unpopulated (None / empty list) — PiperBackend.synthesize_aligned therefore yields no words on that voice and speak_aligned reports the alignment unavailable. The mechanism is implemented and fake-pinned; a voice that populates the fields will flow measured timings through it unchanged.

measured_env: Python 3.12.3; TTS rung: piper via UniversalTTS (piper-tts 1.3.x, voice en_US-lessac-medium 22050 Hz, PIPER_VOICE-pinned); STT rung: STTTranscriber -> UniversalSTT -> faster-whisper 1.2.1, model tiny.en (FASTER_WHISPER_MODEL), CPU int8, word_timestamps on. Scratch venv pins: PyAV 12.3.0 (faster-whisper 1.2.1's decode_audio passes metadata_errors=, a kwarg PyAV removed in later versions — an unpinned av breaks the rung, recorded here so the next measurer does not rediscover it). Floors sit above the measured values by the floor_rule margin; a rung falling under its floor is a regression, not weather.
